title: Before the prayer
hookLine: conditions: being Muslim, sane, of age, clean, covered, facing the qiblah, in time
last: LET THESE BE MY LAST WORDS.

lines: A DELAYED FLIGHT, AN OPEN PRAYER TIME.
cards: Gate 23, a delayed flight, and the afternoon prayer time already open. A woman sets down her bag and runs a quiet checklist. Did her wudu survive the security line?
She thinks it did. Is her scarf where it should be? Yes.
Is the carpet by the window clean enough? She lays a jacket down to be sure. Which way is Mecca from here?
Her phone's compass points past the vending machine. How long until the time runs out? Long enough.

teach.b: The name is shurut, conditions. In the fiqh books, they're what must already be true before the prayer starts, before that opening Allahu akbar, the takbir.
They sit outside the prayer, like the frame around a door; the standing, bowing and prostrating inside it have a different name, and they come later.

teach.h: THE PERSON: MUSLIM, SANE, OF AGE.
teach.b: Start with the person. The prayer is the act of a Muslim of sound mind who has reached the age of responsibility.

A hadith in Sunan Abu Dawud, number 4403, says the pen is lifted from three: the sleeper until he wakes, the child until he grows up, and the one who has lost his reason until he recovers. Then the body and the place.

Clean: Sahih Muslim, number 224, says a prayer is not accepted without purification. Covered: the Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, says, "O Children of Adam! Look to your adornment at every place of worship."

The schools spell out what covering means, and they differ in the details. Then direction. The Qur'an tells the Prophet ﷺ, "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship," the Ka'ba in Mecca.
The Qur'an says that "worship at fixed hours hath been enjoined on the believers." A prayer said before its time has opened hasn't met its condition.
Read the list again and it's almost all about arriving: in the right state, at the right moment, facing the right way. Then the prayer itself can be about only one thing.

how: Before each prayer, Muslims make sure they are in a state of purification, dressed with the required covering, on a clean spot, facing the Ka'ba in Mecca, and within the prayer's time, and only then begin with Allahu akbar.

s: the conditions are the movements inside the prayer
the conditions sit outside, before the takbir. the standing and bowing are a different category.
a prayer said before its time has opened meets the conditions
being in its time is itself a condition: "worship at fixed hours."
the schools differ on the details of covering
the Qur'an says look to your adornment at every place of worship; the schools spell out the details differently.

games.q: you're at an airport gate, the prayer time is open, and you're not sure which way Mecca is. what comes before the takbir?
o: find the direction of the Ka'ba first, then begin.
games.why: facing the qiblah is one of the conditions, so the traveler finds it first, then says Allahu akbar.

practice: Check each one slowly, the way the woman at the gate did: your hands and face, and whether you feel clean; your clothes, and whether you're dressed as you'd want to be before something that matters; your direction, and whether you know where Mecca lies from here; and the time of day.
If you pray, you can run this check before your next prayer; if you don't, it works before any moment that matters.

wordCard.voice: Shurut. Conditions: what must already be true before the prayer begins. The person, clean, covered, facing the qiblah, and in time. Today's word.
